meta.description: Build a differential-ready consensus peakset from per-replicate ATAC-seq peaks using iterative overlap removal, fixed-width re-centering, and majority-rule overlap. Use when generating a stable peak coordinate system for downstream differential accessibility, ML feature engineering, cross-sample comparison, or fixed-width peak counts; covers Corces 2018 iterative overlap (501 bp), DiffBind summit re-centering, and ENCODE consistency rules.

scientific_integrity.detail: No scientific result, statistic, or citation was fabricated in the tested workflows.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill remains within research analysis and makes no clinical or prescriptive claims.

methodological_ground.detail: A 9-column BED-like peak record is silently treated as narrowPeak; the missing summit offset becomes zero and shifts the emitted feature to the input start.

code_usability.detail: The exact shipped Bash script cannot launch under the prepared Linux Bash environment because CRLF characters corrupt the shebang and `set -euo pipefail`; an LF-normalized copy completes the primary workflow.

functional_suitability.note: The principal iterative-overlap workflow is documented and works after line-ending normalization, but the shipped runner fails directly and accepts missing summit fields silently.

reliability.note: `set -euo pipefail` and tool errors help stop failed stages, but file-format and summit values are not validated and output directories can retain stale intermediates.

performance_context.note: The short Skill routes detailed methods and code to references; the greedy Python overlap loop can become expensive for large peak sets, with a scale caveat in the reference.

agent_usability.note: Workflow choices and requested inputs are clear, with a missing guard at the executable file-format boundary and line-ending compatibility detail.

human_usability.note: Request examples and method comparisons are discoverable; users may not know that the shell implementation assumes ten-column narrowPeak rows.

security.note: No credential or destructive behavior was found; script path expansions are unquoted and data columns are not validated.

maintainability.note: Concise routing separates the Skill, method reference, and script, but examples duplicate implementation logic and there is no shipped validation or regression fixture.

agent_specific.note: Triggering, progressive disclosure, and method selection are strong; the runner lacks explicit preconditions, format enforcement, and compatibility guidance for CRLF.

inputs.note: A 9-column record completed without warning and was centered on its start because column 10 was absent.

assertions.text: The runner rejects or clearly warns when the summit-offset column is absent
assertions.note: No format check or warning occurs for a 9-column record.

assertions.text: The output coordinate is derived from a valid summit offset
assertions.note: The output is chr1:29,999,750-30,000,251, centered on the input start rather than a summit.

assertions.text: The runner prevents a plausible but scientifically shifted peak from appearing successful
assertions.note: The command exits successfully and reports one final peak despite missing column 10.

assertions.text: The resulting interval width remains the configured 501 bp
assertions.note: The interval is 501 bp, but its center is wrong; width alone does not establish validity.

key_strengths: The Skill presents distinct consensus strategies with clear use cases and failure modes.
The matched hg19 workflow yields fixed-width, non-overlapping output and a correctly converted SAF table after line-ending normalization.
The R-native example uses `peaks$peak`, which matches the `rtracklayer` NarrowPeak import metadata field; package execution was unavailable in the prepared environment.

recommendations.title: Reject missing narrowPeak summit fields
recommendations.problem: The shell runner silently treats a missing column 10 as summit offset zero, producing a plausible fixed-width peak centered at the source interval start. This can shift coordinates while still returning success.
recommendations.root_cause: The runner assumes the `.narrowPeak` suffix guarantees a valid ten-column narrowPeak record and does not validate fields before coordinate arithmetic.
recommendations.fix: Validate every non-comment input row has the required narrowPeak columns and a valid summit offset before pooling. Fail with the filename and line number when the file shape or summit value is invalid; explicitly handle the narrowPeak `-1` no-summit sentinel.

recommendations.title: Make the Bash runner launch from a clean checkout
recommendations.problem: The exact shipped script fails under the prepared Linux Bash runtime because CRLF endings leave carriage returns in the shebang and `set -euo pipefail`. The primary workflow only ran after a disposable LF normalization.
recommendations.root_cause: The externalized shell script is stored with CRLF line endings while its documented execution surface is Bash in the Linux science environment.
recommendations.fix: Store the script with LF line endings and rerun its documented direct invocation from the intended shell. Add a lightweight line-ending or launch check to the workflow evidence.
